name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: '23 6 * * 1'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  test:
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python: ['3.11', '3.12', '3.13', '3.14']
        resolution: [highest]
        include:
          - python: '3.11'
            resolution: lowest-direct
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
      - name: Install dependencies in a clean environment
        env:
          RESOLUTION: ${{ matrix.resolution }}
        run: |
          uv venv .venv
          uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --resolution "$RESOLUTION" -e '.[dev]'
          uv pip check --python .venv/bin/python
      - run: .venv/bin/python -m pytest
      - if: matrix.python == '3.11' && matrix.resolution == 'highest'
        run: |
          .venv/bin/python -m ruff check .
          .venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check .
          .venv/bin/python -m mypy src
          .venv/bin/python -m build
          .venv/bin/python -m twine check dist/*
          uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --reinstall --no-deps dist/*.whl
          .venv/bin/python -I -c "from strands_e2b import E2BSandbox; print(E2BSandbox.__name__)"

  sdk-compat:
    name: Latest SDK compatibility
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.14'
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0
      - name: Install newest published SDKs
        run: |
          uv venv .venv
          uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -e '.[dev]'
          uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --upgrade strands-agents e2b
          uv pip check --python .venv/bin/python
      - run: |
          .venv/bin/python -m mypy src
          .venv/bin/python -m pytest

name: Publish to PyPI

on:
  release:
    types: [published]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: publish-${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Verify release tag and main ancestry
        env:
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
        run: |
          git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main
          [[ "$RELEASE_TAG" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+((a|b|rc)[0-9]+)?$ ]]
      - run: python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'
      - name: Validate and build distributions
        env:
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
        run: |
          python -m ruff check .
          python -m ruff format --check .
          python -m mypy src
          python -m pytest
          python -m build
          python -m twine check dist/*
          ls dist/*-"${RELEASE_TAG#v}"-py3-none-any.whl
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: distributions
          path: dist/
          if-no-files-found: error

  publish:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: pypi
      url: https://pypi.org/project/strands-e2b/
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: distributions
          path: dist/
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@dc37677b2e1c63e2034f94d8a5b11f265b73ba33 # v1.14.2

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling>=1.27", "hatch-vcs>=0.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "strands-e2b"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "E2B sandboxes for Strands Agents: run an agent's shell, Python, and file tools in an isolated cloud sandbox."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = "MIT"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
authors = [{ name = "e2b", email = "hello@e2b.dev" }]
keywords = ["strands", "strands-agents", "e2b", "sandbox", "agents", "code-interpreter"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
dependencies = ["strands-agents>=1.64.0,<2", "e2b>=2.63.0,<3"]

[project.urls]
Repository = "https://github.com/e2b-dev/strands-e2b"
Documentation = "https://github.com/e2b-dev/strands-e2b#readme"
Issues = "https://github.com/e2b-dev/strands-e2b/issues"

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8,<10",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1,<2",
    "pytest-timeout>=2,<3",
    "ruff>=0.16,<0.17",
    "mypy>=1.15,<2.4",
    "build>=1,<2",
    "twine>=7,<8",
]

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"

[tool.hatch.version.raw-options]
tag_regex = '^v(?P<version>[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(?:(?:a|b|rc)[0-9]+)?)$'
git_describe_command = "git describe --dirty --tags --long --match v[0-9]*"
fallback_version = "0.0.0"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/strands_e2b"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
only-include = ["src", "tests", "examples", "README.md", "LICENSE", "pyproject.toml"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "strict"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
addopts = "--strict-markers -m 'not live'"
markers = ["live: needs E2B_API_KEY and creates a real E2B sandbox"]
timeout = 30

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "B", "UP", "ASYNC"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
strict = true
follow_imports = "silent"

"""Run a Strands agent whose shell, Python, and file tools execute in E2B.

Requires E2B_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, plus:
    pip install strands-e2b "strands-agents[anthropic]"
"""

import asyncio

from e2b import AsyncSandbox
from strands import Agent
from strands.models.anthropic import AnthropicModel

from strands_e2b import E2BSandbox

PROMPT = "Write a CSV with the squares of 1..10 to squares.csv, then use Python to print the sum of the squares column."


async def main() -> None:
    # You own the sandbox: create it, and kill it when the agent is done.
    sandbox = await AsyncSandbox.create(timeout=600)
    try:
        agent = Agent(
            model=AnthropicModel(model_id="claude-haiku-5-5", max_tokens=4096),
            sandbox=E2BSandbox(sandbox, working_dir="/home/user"),
        )
        result = await agent.invoke_async(PROMPT)
        print(result)
        print((await agent.sandbox.read_text("squares.csv")).splitlines()[:3])
    finally:
        await sandbox.kill()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

# strands-e2b

Run a [Strands Agents](https://strandsagents.com/) agent's shell, Python, and file tools in an [E2B](https://e2b.dev/) sandbox instead of on your machine.

`E2BSandbox` plugs into Strands' native sandbox API (`Agent(sandbox=...)`). You create the E2B sandbox and pass it in; the agent's shell, Python, and file tools then run inside it, and you kill it when you're done.

## Install

Requires Python 3.11 or later.

```sh
pip install strands-e2b
```

Set `E2B_API_KEY` ([get one](https://e2b.dev/dashboard?tab=keys)) and the credentials for your Strands model provider.

## Use with an agent

The example uses Claude Haiku through Strands' Anthropic provider (`pip install "strands-agents[anthropic]"`, plus `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). Any Strands model works.

```python
import asyncio

from e2b import AsyncSandbox
from strands import Agent
from strands.models.anthropic import AnthropicModel

from strands_e2b import E2BSandbox


async def main() -> None:
    # You own the sandbox: create it, and kill it when the agent is done.
    sandbox = await AsyncSandbox.create(timeout=600)
    try:
        agent = Agent(
            model=AnthropicModel(model_id="claude-haiku-5-5", max_tokens=4096),
            sandbox=E2BSandbox(sandbox, working_dir="/home/user"),
        )
        await agent.invoke_async(
            "Write a CSV with the squares of 1..10 to squares.csv, "
            "then use Python to print the sum of the squares column."
        )
        print(await agent.sandbox.read_text("squares.csv"))
    finally:
        await sandbox.kill()


asyncio.run(main())
```

The agent writes `squares.csv` inside the sandbox and answers 385. A runnable version is in [examples/agent.py](examples/agent.py) (`python examples/agent.py`). Synchronous calls (`agent("...")`) work too.

## Tools

`E2BSandbox` registers these Strands tools, bound to the sandbox:

| Tool | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `sandbox_shell` | Runs a shell command |
| `sandbox_python_repl` | Runs Python code in a fresh `python3` process |
| `sandbox_read` | Reads a file (text, images, documents) |
| `sandbox_write` | Creates or overwrites a file |
| `sandbox_edit` | Replaces an exact string in a file |

`Agent(sandbox=...)` always registers all five; a tool you pass yourself with the same name takes precedence. To give the agent fewer tools, don't pass `sandbox=`. Instead pass tools bound to the sandbox, for example `Agent(tools=[make_read(sandbox=E2BSandbox(sandbox))])` with `make_read` from `strands.vended_tools`. In that setup `agent.sandbox` and any other Strands tools you add run on your machine.

You can also drive the sandbox from your own code, for example to seed input files or read results:

```python
s = E2BSandbox(sandbox, working_dir="/home/user")
await s.write_text("input.txt", "hello")
result = await s.execute("wc -c input.txt")
print(result.exit_code, result.stdout)
```

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox` | required | A running `e2b.AsyncSandbox` |
| `working_dir` | E2B default (`/home/user`) | Absolute directory for commands and relative file paths. The directory must exist. |
| `user` | E2B default | E2B user for commands and file operations. File operations go through the E2B filesystem API, which is not limited by this user's permissions. |

## Behavior and lifecycle

- **You own the sandbox.** `E2BSandbox` never creates, pauses, extends, or kills it. Strands does not close it either. Kill it yourself, and keep the E2B sandbox `timeout` longer than the agent run.
- **Files persist, processes don't.** Files stay in the sandbox for its lifetime and are shared by all tools. Each command and each Python call starts a fresh process, so shell variables, `cd`, and Python variables don't carry over. Save intermediate results to files.
- **Commands** run with `bash -l -c` in `working_dir` (or the per-call `cwd`) and stream stdout and stderr. A non-zero exit code is returned as a result, not raised. `env` values are passed to the command as is. Your local environment, including `E2B_API_KEY`, is never forwarded.
- **Timeouts.** A tool's `timeout` is a wall-clock limit. When it expires, the command is killed and Strands' `SandboxTimeoutError` is raised with the output so far.
- **Killing a command** sends `SIGKILL` to its whole process group: the shell, pipelines, child processes such as `python3`, and `&` jobs. This happens on timeout, cancellation, closing the output stream early, and a dropped connection. A process that starts its own session (`setsid`, daemons) is not reached. Without `setsid` in the template, only the shell is killed.
- **Uncertain outcomes.** If the connection drops while a command is starting, or the kill request fails (it is logged as a warning), the command may still be running. It is never retried automatically.
- **File operations** use the E2B filesystem API, so binary files and large files work without shell encoding. Parent directories are created on write. Missing paths raise `FileNotFoundError`, reading a directory raises `IsADirectoryError`, and listing a file raises `NotADirectoryError`. Other E2B errors keep their E2B exception type.
- **Output is not truncated by the adapter.** Commands keep their full output in memory, as Strands expects. Redirect very large output to a file.
- **Isolation comes from the sandbox.** `working_dir` is not a boundary. In the default E2B template the `user` account has passwordless `sudo`, so anything the agent runs can reach the whole sandbox, but not your machine. Network access follows the sandbox's settings (`AsyncSandbox.create(allow_internet_access=...)`).
- **Strands harness.** `create_harness(sandbox=E2BSandbox(...))` works too: the harness replaces the `sandbox_*` tools with its own `shell`, `read`, `write`, and `edit`, which run in the sandbox. Its session and memory files stay on your machine.
- Tools run concurrently by default in Strands. Concurrent edits of the same file are not coordinated.

## Development

```sh
uv venv && uv pip install -e '.[dev]'
pytest                       # mocked tests, no credentials needed
E2B_API_KEY=... pytest -m live   # creates real E2B sandboxes
ruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy src
```

"""Live checks against a real E2B sandbox.

Run with ``E2B_API_KEY`` set: ``pytest -m live``. Each test creates and kills
its own sandbox. Not part of the default (mocked) test run.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import os
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator

import pytest
import pytest_asyncio
from e2b import AsyncSandbox
from strands.sandbox.errors import SandboxTimeoutError

from strands_e2b import E2BSandbox

pytestmark = [
    pytest.mark.live,
    pytest.mark.timeout(180),
    pytest.mark.skipif(not os.environ.get("E2B_API_KEY"), reason="E2B_API_KEY not set"),
]

WORK = "/home/user/work"


@pytest_asyncio.fixture
async def sbx() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSandbox]:
    sandbox = await AsyncSandbox.create(timeout=300, metadata={"purpose": "strands-e2b-live-test"})
    try:
        await sandbox.files.make_dir(WORK)
        yield sandbox
    finally:
        await sandbox.kill()


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_commands_and_files_share_the_workspace(sbx: AsyncSandbox) -> None:
    s = E2BSandbox(sbx, working_dir=WORK)

    assert (await s.execute("pwd")).stdout.strip() == WORK
    assert (await s.execute("echo from-shell > shell.txt")).exit_code == 0
    assert await s.read_text("shell.txt") == "from-shell\n"
    assert await s.read_text(f"{WORK}/shell.txt") == "from-shell\n"

    await s.write_text("nested/dir/api.txt", "from-api")
    assert (await s.execute("cat nested/dir/api.txt")).stdout == "from-api"
    assert (await s.execute("pwd", cwd="/tmp")).stdout.strip() == "/tmp"


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_binary_round_trip_and_listing(sbx: AsyncSandbox) -> None:
    s = E2BSandbox(sbx, working_dir=WORK)
    payload = bytes(range(256)) * 4096  # 1 MiB
    await s.write_file("blob.bin", payload)

    assert await s.read_file("blob.bin") == payload
    assert (await s.execute("sha256sum blob.bin")).exit_code == 0
    await s.write_text(".hidden", "")
    entries = {e.name: e for e in await s.list_files(WORK)}
    assert entries["blob.bin"].size == len(payload) and entries["blob.bin"].is_dir is False
    assert ".hidden" in entries


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_missing_paths_and_directory_errors(sbx: AsyncSandbox) -> None:
    s = E2BSandbox(sbx, working_dir=WORK)
    with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
        await s.read_file("missing.txt")
    with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
        await s.remove_file("missing.txt")
    with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
        await s.list_files("missing-dir")
    with pytest.raises(IsADirectoryError):
        await s.remove_file(WORK)

    await s.write_text("gone.txt", "x")
    await s.remove_file("gone.txt")
    assert (await s.execute("test -e gone.txt")).exit_code == 1


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_wrong_kind_of_path_errors(sbx: AsyncSandbox) -> None:
    s = E2BSandbox(sbx, working_dir=WORK)
    with pytest.raises(IsADirectoryError):
        await s.read_file(WORK)
    with pytest.raises(NotADirectoryError):
        await s.list_files("/etc/hostname")


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_files_api_is_not_limited_by_user_permissions(sbx: AsyncSandbox) -> None:
    """Documents E2B behavior the README relies on: `user` does not confine file access."""
    s = E2BSandbox(sbx, user="user")
    assert (await s.execute("cat /etc/shadow")).exit_code != 0
    assert await s.read_file("/etc/shadow")


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_env_exit_code_and_code_execution(sbx: AsyncSandbox) -> None:
    s = E2BSandbox(sbx, working_dir=WORK)

    r = await s.execute('printf %s "$A"; echo err >&2; exit 3', env={"A": "x y; $(z) 'q'"})
    assert (r.exit_code, r.stdout, r.stderr) == (3, "x y; $(z) 'q'", "err\n")

    r = await s.execute_code("import os; print(os.getcwd()); print(1 + 1)", "python3")
    assert r.stdout == f"{WORK}\n2\n"

    r = await s.execute_code("x = 1", "python3")
    r = await s.execute_code("print('x' in globals())", "python3")
    assert r.stdout == "False\n"  # fresh interpreter per call


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_no_timeout_runs_past_e2b_default_stream_deadline(sbx: AsyncSandbox) -> None:
    s = E2BSandbox(sbx)
    r = await s.execute("sleep 65; echo done", timeout=None)
    assert (r.exit_code, r.stdout) == (0, "done\n")


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_timeout_kills_the_whole_process_group(sbx: AsyncSandbox) -> None:
    s = E2BSandbox(sbx)
    cmd = "echo started; (sleep 3; touch /tmp/background) & sleep 3 | cat; touch /tmp/foreground"

    with pytest.raises(SandboxTimeoutError) as info:
        await s.execute(cmd, timeout=1)
    assert info.value.stdout == "started\n"

    await asyncio.sleep(4)
    assert (await s.execute("ls /tmp/background /tmp/foreground")).exit_code == 2  # neither exists
    assert (await s.execute("pgrep -x sleep")).exit_code == 1


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_timeout_kills_processes_started_with_sudo(sbx: AsyncSandbox) -> None:
    s = E2BSandbox(sbx)
    with pytest.raises(SandboxTimeoutError):
        await s.execute("sudo sleep 30", timeout=1)
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    assert (await s.execute("pgrep -x sleep")).exit_code == 1


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_commands_run_in_a_login_shell(sbx: AsyncSandbox) -> None:
    r = await E2BSandbox(sbx).execute("shopt -q login_shell && echo login")
    assert r.stdout == "login\n"


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_template_without_setsid_still_runs_and_times_out(sbx: AsyncSandbox) -> None:
    s = E2BSandbox(sbx)
    assert (await s.execute("sudo mv $(command -v setsid) /tmp/setsid.bak")).exit_code == 0
    r = await s.execute("echo hi; exit 4")
    assert (r.exit_code, r.stdout) == (4, "hi\n")
    with pytest.raises(SandboxTimeoutError):
        await s.execute("sleep 30", timeout=1)
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    assert (await s.execute("pgrep -x sleep")).exit_code == 1  # the shell exec'd sleep, so the kill reached it


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_timeout_stops_python_code(sbx: AsyncSandbox) -> None:
    s = E2BSandbox(sbx)
    code = "import time; print('started', flush=True); time.sleep(3); open('/tmp/py-marker', 'w').close()"

    with pytest.raises(SandboxTimeoutError) as info:
        await s.execute_code(code, "python3", timeout=1)
    assert info.value.stdout == "started\n"

    await asyncio.sleep(4)
    assert (await s.execute("test -e /tmp/py-marker")).exit_code == 1
    assert (await s.execute("pgrep -x python3")).exit_code == 1


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_cancellation_kills_remote_command(sbx: AsyncSandbox) -> None:
    s = E2BSandbox(sbx)
    task = asyncio.create_task(s.execute_code("import time; time.sleep(3); open('/tmp/cancel-marker', 'w')", "python3"))
    await asyncio.sleep(1.5)
    task.cancel()
    with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
        await task

    await asyncio.sleep(3)
    assert (await s.execute("test -e /tmp/cancel-marker")).exit_code == 1


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_overlapping_commands_cancel_only_one(sbx: AsyncSandbox) -> None:
    s = E2BSandbox(sbx)
    victim = asyncio.create_task(s.execute("sleep 3; touch /tmp/victim"))
    survivor = asyncio.create_task(s.execute("sleep 3; touch /tmp/survivor; echo ok"))
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    victim.cancel()

    assert (await survivor).stdout == "ok\n"
    with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
        await victim
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    assert (await s.execute("test -e /tmp/victim")).exit_code == 1
    assert (await s.execute("test -e /tmp/survivor")).exit_code == 0


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_sandbox_lifecycle_is_untouched(sbx: AsyncSandbox) -> None:
    s = E2BSandbox(sbx, working_dir=WORK)
    before = (await sbx.get_info()).end_at
    s.get_tools()
    await s.execute("true")
    assert await sbx.is_running()
    assert (await sbx.get_info()).end_at == before

"""Unit tests for E2BSandbox.

Commands use the real ``e2b`` ``AsyncCommandHandle`` fed with scripted process
events, so stream, exit-code, and wait semantics come from the installed SDK.
Only the transport (events, kill RPC) and the filesystem are faked.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import gc
import logging
import os
import shlex
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any

import pytest
from e2b import FileNotFoundException, FileType, InvalidArgumentException, SandboxUnreachableException
from e2b.envd.process import process_pb as p
from e2b.sandbox.filesystem.filesystem import EntryInfo
from e2b.sandbox_async.commands.command_handle import AsyncCommandHandle
from protobuf import Oneof
from strands import Agent
from strands.sandbox import ExecutionResult, StreamChunk
from strands.sandbox.errors import SandboxTimeoutError

from strands_e2b import E2BSandbox

_E = p.ProcessEvent


def out(stream: str, data: bytes) -> p.StartResponse:
    return p.StartResponse(
        event=_E(event=Oneof(field="data", value=_E.DataEvent(output=Oneof(field=stream, value=data))))
    )


def end(code: int) -> p.StartResponse:
    return p.StartResponse(
        event=_E(event=Oneof(field="end", value=_E.EndEvent(exit_code=code, exited=True, status="")))
    )


class FakeCommands:
    """Starts real command handles over scripted events; records calls and kills."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.events: asyncio.Queue[Any] = asyncio.Queue()
        self.run_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {}
        self.kills = 0
        self.group_kills: list[str] = []
        self.kill_error: Exception | None = None
        self.started = asyncio.Event()

    def script(self, *events: Any) -> None:
        for e in events:
            self.events.put_nowait(e)

    async def _stream(self) -> Any:
        while True:
            item = await self.events.get()
            if isinstance(item, Exception):
                raise item
            yield item
            if item is not None and item.event.event.field == "end":
                return

    async def _kill(self) -> bool:
        self.kills += 1
        if self.kill_error:
            raise self.kill_error
        # Like envd: the killed process reports its end on the stream.
        self.script(end(-1))
        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
        return True

    async def run(self, cmd: str, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        if cmd.startswith("kill -KILL"):
            assert kwargs["user"] == "root"
            self.group_kills.append(cmd)
            if self.kill_error:
                raise self.kill_error
            return None
        self.run_kwargs = {"cmd": cmd, **kwargs}
        self.started.set()
        return AsyncCommandHandle(
            7, self._kill, self._stream(), on_stdout=kwargs["on_stdout"], on_stderr=kwargs["on_stderr"]
        )


def entry(name: str, type_: FileType, size: int = 0) -> EntryInfo:
    return EntryInfo(
        name=name,
        path=f"/x/{name}",
        type=type_,
        size=size,
        mode=0,
        permissions="",
        owner="",
        group="",
        modified_time=datetime(2026, 1, 1),
    )


class FakeFiles:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.data: dict[str, bytes] = {}
        self.dirs: dict[str, list[EntryInfo]] = {}
        self.removed: list[str] = []
        self.users: list[str | None] = []

    async def read(self, path: str, format: str, user: str | None = None) -> bytearray:
        self.users.append(user)
        if path in self.dirs:
            raise InvalidArgumentException(f"path '{path}' is a directory")
        if path == "/bad":
            raise InvalidArgumentException("invalid path")
        if path not in self.data:
            raise FileNotFoundException(path)
        return bytearray(self.data[path])

    async def write(self, path: str, data: bytes, user: str | None = None) -> None:
        self.users.append(user)
        self.data[path] = data

    async def get_info(self, path: str, user: str | None = None) -> EntryInfo:
        if path in self.dirs:
            return entry(path, FileType.DIR)
        if path in self.data:
            return entry(path, FileType.FILE)
        raise FileNotFoundException(path)

    async def remove(self, path: str, user: str | None = None) -> None:
        self.removed.append(path)
        self.data.pop(path, None)

    async def list(self, path: str, depth: int, user: str | None = None) -> list[EntryInfo]:
        assert depth == 1
        if path in self.data:
            raise InvalidArgumentException(f"path is not a directory: {path}")
        if path not in self.dirs:
            raise FileNotFoundException(path)
        return self.dirs[path]

    sandbox_id = "sbx-test"

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.commands = FakeCommands()

"""Strands sandbox backed by an E2B sandbox."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
import posixpath
import shlex
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator, Callable
from typing import Any

from e2b import AsyncSandbox, CommandExitException, FileNotFoundException, FileType, InvalidArgumentException
from strands.sandbox import ExecutionResult, FileInfo, PosixShellSandbox, StreamChunk
from strands.sandbox.errors import SandboxPathNotFoundError, SandboxTimeoutError
from strands.sandbox.posix_shell import validate_env_keys
from strands.types.tools import AgentTool
from strands.vended_tools import make_edit, make_python_repl, make_read, make_shell, make_write

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Upper bound for the kill request sent when a command is cancelled or times out.
_KILL_TIMEOUT = 10.0
_DONE = object()


def _on_done(queue: asyncio.Queue[Any]) -> Callable[[asyncio.Future[Any]], None]:
    """Wake the consumer when the command ends.

    Also marks the outcome as retrieved: after a kill the command ends with an
    exit error that nobody reads, which asyncio would otherwise log.
    """

    def callback(future: asyncio.Future[Any]) -> None:
        if not future.cancelled():
            future.exception()
        queue.put_nowait(_DONE)

    return callback


class E2BSandbox(PosixShellSandbox):
    """Run a Strands agent's shell, code, and file operations in an E2B sandbox.

    The sandbox is borrowed: you create it, keep it alive, and kill it. This
    class never creates, pauses, extends, or kills the E2B sandbox.

    Commands run through ``sandbox.commands.run`` and stream their output.
    Code runs through the inherited :class:`PosixShellSandbox` path, so each
    call starts a fresh interpreter. Files use the E2B filesystem API.

    Args:
        sandbox: A running ``e2b.AsyncSandbox``.
        working_dir: Absolute directory for commands and relative file paths.
            ``None`` uses the E2B user's default directory.
        user: E2B user for commands and file operations. ``None`` uses the
            sandbox default.
    """

    def __init__(self, sandbox: AsyncSandbox, *, working_dir: str | None = None, user: str | None = None) -> None:
        if working_dir is not None and not posixpath.isabs(working_dir):
            raise ValueError(f"working_dir must be an absolute path, got {working_dir!r}")
        self.sandbox = sandbox
        self.working_dir = working_dir
        self.user = user

    async def execute_streaming(
        self,
        command: str,
        *,
        timeout: float | None = None,  # noqa: ASYNC109 - required by the Strands Sandbox interface
        cwd: str | None = None,
        env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> AsyncGenerator[StreamChunk | ExecutionResult, None]:
        """Run a shell command in the E2B sandbox and stream its output.

        ``timeout`` is a wall-clock deadline enforced here. When it expires, or
        when the caller cancels or closes the stream, the remote command is
        killed. A non-zero exit code is returned as a result, not raised.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If an environment variable name is invalid.
            SandboxTimeoutError: If the command runs longer than ``timeout``.
        """
        if env:
            validate_env_keys(env)

        deadline = None if timeout is None else asyncio.get_running_loop().time() + timeout
        queue: asyncio.Queue[Any] = asyncio.Queue()

        handle = await self.sandbox.commands.run(
            # setsid (when the template has it) makes the command's shell lead a new
            # process group, so a kill also stops pipelines, children, and `&` jobs.
            f"exec $(command -v setsid) /bin/bash -l -c {shlex.quote(command)}",
            background=True,
            envs=env,
            cwd=cwd if cwd is not None else self.working_dir,
            user=self.user,
            on_stdout=lambda data: queue.put_nowait(StreamChunk(data, "stdout")),
            on_stderr=lambda data: queue.put_nowait(StreamChunk(data, "stderr")),
            # None disables E2B's stream deadline (60 s by default); the command
            # deadline is enforced below, where it can kill the process.
            timeout=None,
        )
        waiter = asyncio.ensure_future(handle.wait())
        waiter.add_done_callback(_on_done(queue))
        finished = False

        try:
            while True:
                try:
                    async with asyncio.timeout_at(deadline):
                        item = await queue.get()
                except TimeoutError:
                    raise SandboxTimeoutError(timeout, handle.stdout or "", handle.stderr or "") from None
                if item is _DONE:
                    break
                yield item

            try:
                result = waiter.result()
            except CommandExitException as e:
                finished = True
                yield ExecutionResult(exit_code=e.exit_code, stdout=e.stdout, stderr=e.stderr)
            else:
                finished = True
                yield ExecutionResult(exit_code=result.exit_code, stdout=result.stdout, stderr=result.stderr)
        finally:
            # Timeout, cancellation, an early close, or a dropped stream: the command
            # may still be running remotely.
            if not finished:
                await self._kill(handle)
            await handle.disconnect()

    async def _kill(self, handle: Any) -> None:
        """Kill a command and its process group, logging (not raising) on failure."""
        try:
            await asyncio.shield(asyncio.wait_for(self._kill_group(handle), _KILL_TIMEOUT))
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            raise
        except Exception as e:
            # The command may still be running; say so instead of failing silently.
            logger.warning("pid=<%s>, error=<%s> | failed to kill E2B command", handle.pid, type(e).__name__)

    async def _kill_group(self, handle: Any) -> None:
        try:
            # As root, so processes the command started with sudo are reached too.
            await self.sandbox.commands.run(f"kill -KILL -- -{handle.pid}", user="root", timeout=_KILL_TIMEOUT)
        except CommandExitException:
            pass  # no such group: already gone, or setsid was unavailable
        await handle.kill()  # the shell itself, in case the group kill could not reach it

    def _path(self, path: str) -> str:
        if self.working_dir is not None and not posixpath.isabs(path):
            return posixpath.join(self.working_dir, path)
        return path

    async def _is_dir(self, target: str) -> bool:
        try:
            return (await self.sandbox.files.get_info(target, user=self.user)).type == FileType.DIR
        except FileNotFoundException:
            return False

    async def read_file(self, path: str, **kwargs: Any) -> bytes:
        """Read a file from the E2B sandbox as bytes.

        Raises:
            FileNotFoundError: If the file does not exist.
            IsADirectoryError: If ``path`` is a directory.
        """
        target = self._path(path)
        try:
            data = await self.sandbox.files.read(target, format="bytes", user=self.user)
        except FileNotFoundException:
            raise SandboxPathNotFoundError(path) from None
        except InvalidArgumentException:
            # E2B reports a directory as an invalid argument; Strands expects IsADirectoryError.
            if await self._is_dir(target):
                raise IsADirectoryError(path) from None
            raise
        return bytes(data)

    async def write_file(self, path: str, content: bytes, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        """Write bytes to a file in the E2B sandbox, creating parent directories."""
        await self.sandbox.files.write(self._path(path), content, user=self.user)

    async def remove_file(self, path: str, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        """Remove a file from the E2B sandbox.

        Raises:
            FileNotFoundError: If the file does not exist.
            IsADirectoryError: If ``path`` is a directory.
        """
        target = self._path(path)
        # E2B removal succeeds for missing paths and removes directories, while
        # Strands expects FileNotFoundError and file-only removal. The check is
        # not atomic with the removal.
        try:
            info = await self.sandbox.files.get_info(target, user=self.user)
        except FileNotFoundException:
            raise SandboxPathNotFoundError(path) from None
        if info.type == FileType.DIR:
            raise IsADirectoryError(path)
        await self.sandbox.files.remove(target, user=self.user)

    async def list_files(self, path: str, **kwargs: Any) -> list[FileInfo]:
        """List the immediate entries of a directory in the E2B sandbox.

        Raises:
            FileNotFoundError: If the directory does not exist.
            NotADirectoryError: If ``path`` is not a directory.
        """
        target = self._path(path)
        try:
            entries = await self.sandbox.files.list(target, depth=1, user=self.user)
        except FileNotFoundException:
            raise SandboxPathNotFoundError(path) from None
        except InvalidArgumentException:
            if not await self._is_dir(target):
                raise NotADirectoryError(path) from None
            raise
        return [FileInfo(name=e.name, is_dir=e.type == FileType.DIR, size=e.size) for e in entries]

    def get_tools(self) -> list[AgentTool]:
        """Shell, Python, and file tools bound to this sandbox."""
        where = f" Runs in E2B sandbox {self.sandbox.sandbox_id}."
        if self.working_dir:
            where += f" Working directory: {self.working_dir}."
        tools: list[AgentTool] = [
            make_shell(sandbox=self, name="sandbox_shell"),
            make_python_repl(sandbox=self, name="sandbox_python_repl"),
            make_read(sandbox=self, name="sandbox_read"),
            make_write(sandbox=self, name="sandbox_write"),
            make_edit(sandbox=self, name="sandbox_edit"),
        ]
        for tool in tools:
            tool.tool_spec["description"] += where
        return tools

"""E2B sandboxes for Strands Agents."""
